annotates.body:
1  Python exe -> a python 3.11 or newer that has open3d.
   Pulse Check worker and wait for OK.

2  Inputs op -> one base COMP holding your camera TOPs.
   Name them after the device type, numbered from 1:
   kinectazure1, orbbec1, zed1 ... one TOP per camera.
   Pin each to its own camera: Sensor on the Kinect TOP,
   Device on the Orbbec TOP, Camera on the ZED TOP.
   Orbbec: set Depth Align Mode to Hardware or Software,
   or the colours will not sit on the points.
   ZED: set Reference Frame to Camera, not World.
   Custom TOPs instead: one customSources row per camera,
   naming a point cloud TOP and a colour TOP inside that
   same base.
   Pick your Device type, then pulse Gather devices.

3  Specify pair: the first camera stays still,
   the second one moves onto it.

4  Pulse Calibrate. Watch the viewport: the two clouds
   should land on each other.

5  Three or more cameras: calibrate each one against its
   NEIGHBOUR (1-2, then 2-3, then 3-4). Not all against 1.

6  Refine polishes a calibration that is already close.
   Reset calibration starts over.

Output is out_pop: every camera in one space, colour included.

Last status only means the solver finished. It does not mean
the answer is right. Only the viewport tells you that. If it
says UNSTABLE, pulse Calibrate again.

All the best,
Darien
